name: Geostationary Imager Observation Parser Node
description: Parser flow node (typed contracts 1.0) for geostationary imager observations from the anonymous public open-data buckets (GOES ABI L1b/L2 NetCDF4, NOAA Open Data Dissemination). parse turns each fetched file into its field's world product: the area mean of the native fixed-grid pixels in each cell of a 4096 x 2048 latitude/longitude grid (limb cells the field sampled at the cell centre; cloud phase the pixel nearest the cell centre), at 4096, 2048 and 1024 wide, one size-prefixed $WXF record per 64-row band, quantized at the instrument's precision and coded as SDS 1.238 defines (InlineEncodedChunk delta/zigzag/shuffle for the smooth fields, InlineQuantizedUint16/Uint8 otherwise), with sensor, channel, platform and scan-time fields. One satellite's fields, never blended or corrected (owner 2026-10-07: SDN carries raw per-satellite fields; the display derives the rest). NetCDF4 is read by the vendored hdf5mini (deflate via the vendored miniz 3.1.2, shuffle) with netCDF4's mask-and-scale; a 0.5 km band is reduced to its 2 km block means chunk by chunk. A file fetched as byte ranges arrives as consecutive parts and is joined first. Input: the HttpResponses (HRSP) of the file's GETs, each echoing in CONTEXT the size-prefixed $WXF header record that is its file job (FIELD_ID, VARIABLE_NAME, SENSOR_ID, DATASET_ID, SOURCE_URL, ORIGIN_ID, LICENSE_URL, CITATION, VALID_TIME_MS, TILE_INDEX/TILE_COUNT); output: the $WXF band stream and an IngestRequest (INGQ). Widths from node config imager_widths (plugin.getConfig, SDS $PIV builtin). No JSON. Values match the reference producer (Cesium_Weather tools/raw_satellite.py) in every float and code on full-disk GOES-18/19 files; tests hold its output for real mesoscale files. capabilities: none, so the node runs in the browser and on WasmEdge alike.

sequentialJustification.detail: parse is a single-pass transform over the frames the flow hands it: each file is read once, chunk by chunk, into one field and its world product, and each band becomes one record. No shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest; the fan-out across files is the flow's, through the http connector node. This guest never spawns a thread, so it compiles wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.displayName: Parse Imager Files into $WXF World Bands
methods.description: Each file's HttpResponse(s) (the file job echoed in CONTEXT; byte-range parts of one file consecutive) -> the field's world product at the configured widths as size-prefixed $WXF band records, plus one IngestRequest for the batch (provider noaa-goes, source <bucket>-world, batch id = SHA-256 of the fetched file bytes, reconcile Duplicates, provenance). A missing part, a response without its job, a non-200 (206 for a ranged part) status or an unreadable file is refused with a named error, never guessed.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP): STATUS, HEADERS, the NetCDF4 BODY verbatim (or a byte range of it), CONTEXT the file job (a size-prefixed $WXF header record).

inputPorts.description: One HttpResponse per file part, in emission order; each carries its own job.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (INGQ) for the $WXF batch: SCHEMA, TAGS, RECONCILE Duplicates, PROVENANCE.
Size-prefixed $WXF FlatBuffer record stream, one record per world band (64 rows) per width per field.
